**Exploring Temporal Variables**

FUNCTIONING DAYS

```{r}
bike_data %>%
  count(Functioning.Day)

bike_data %>%
  group_by(Functioning.Day)%>%
  summarise(mean_func = mean(Rented.Bike.Count, na.rm = TRUE))

bike_data %>%
  drop_na(Rented.Bike.Count, Functioning.Day) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Functioning.Day, fill = Functioning.Day)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("No" = "salmon",
                               "Yes" = "skyblue")) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(x = "Functioning Day",
       y = "Bike Renting Day",
       title = "Relationship between Rental and Functioning Day") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

From the data it can be determined that there were 295 instances of non functioning hours of the Seoul Bike Rental Service between 2017 and 2018, suggesting 12.3 days of the year the bikes were out of commission. This is approximately 3.36% of the year where bikes were unavailable to be rented.

This causes a significant drop in mean bike rentals inclusive and exclusive of the non-functioning days, where bike rental is 0. On functioning days only, the mean is 729.157 rentals per hour, however throughout the whole year the rental rate is 704.602 rentals per hour.


**Exploring Further**
Testing for significance

TESTING 

H0: μ = 729.157
H1: μ < 729.157

Bootstrapping:
  
99% significance z=

sd = 645.998

As we have found that this causes a significant chnage to the mean we will continue by discarding all data points of non-functioning days to remove this confounding variable from other variable investigations. 





HOLIDAYS 

```{r}
bike_data%>%
  group_by(Holiday)%>%
  summarise( 
          min_rent = min(Rented.Bike.Count),
          avg_rent = mean(Rented.Bike.Count, na.rm= TRUE),
          med_rent = median(Rented.Bike.Count),
          max_rent = max(Rented.Bike.Count),
          sd_rent = sd(Rented.Bike.Count),
          quantile(probs = 0.25, Rented.Bike.Count),
          quantile(probs = 0.5, Rented.Bike.Count),
          quantile(probs = 0.75, Rented.Bike.Count))
```
From the data we can see on average that the number of bike rentals decrease during holidays from a mean of 715.2280 to 499.7569, this is significant as it suggests that the majority of rentals perhaps are related to comuttors travel to and from work/ school, further suggesting that rentals mainly occur among the working-aged demographic.

This significant higher rental rates on no holidays are significant on all of the statistics. 

This perhaps suggest the Seoul government should campaign to increase bike rentals on holiday days more. 

```{r}
bike_data %>%
  drop_na(Rented.Bike.Count,Holiday) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Holiday, y = Rented.Bike.Count)) +
  geom_boxplot(color = "blue",
               fill = "skyblue") +
  labs(x = "Holiday",
       y = "Rented Bike Count",
       title = "Relaionship between Rental and Holidays") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

However from the graph, it also becomes apparent that there are many more outliers on non-holiday says. This could suggest bike rentals vary perhaps more greatly on these days as suggested by the greater standard deviation of 646.8791 to 570.7728.

Peraps in future it may be prudent to explore the clientel of bike renters in Seoul or even the concentration of rentals around Soeul to ensure bikes are available in the most relavant locations.

SEASONS

Through these statistics it can be determined that Summer has the greatest average bike rentals and Winter the fewest which is about a fifth of summers rental average- 21.8% (1030.0734 and 225.5412). This is consistent in the median rent also. Standard dev. ...
This may be correlated with weather factors associated with the seasons that we shall explore later.

**Further Explorations**


RAINFALL + TEMP + RENT
Predicting the LINEAR REGGRESSION

```{r}

bike_data_rain <- bike_data %>%
  select(
    Temperature.蚓.,
    Rainfall.mm.,
    Snowfall..cm.,
    Rented.Bike.Count) %>%
  drop_na()

bike_data_rain <- bike_data_rain %>%
  mutate(
    Precipitation = case_when(
      Rainfall.mm. > 0 | Snowfall..cm. > 0 ~ "Precipitation",
      TRUE ~ "No Precipitation"),
    Precipitation = factor(
      Precipitation,
      levels = c("No Precipitation", "Precipitation")))

Bike_data_rain_lm <- linear_reg() %>%
  set_engine("lm") %>%
  fit(Rented.Bike.Count ~ Temperature.蚓.,
    data = bike_data_rain)

tidy(Bike_data_rain_lm)

bike_data_rain %>%
  ggplot(aes(
    x = Temperature.蚓.,
    y = Rented.Bike.Count)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title = "Bike Rentals Based on Temperature",
    x = "Temperature",
    y = "Bike Rentals") +
  theme_minimal()

glance(Bike_data_rain_lm)


Bike_data_rain_lm_engine <- extract_fit_engine(
  Bike_data_rain_lm)

Bike_data_rain_lm_aug <- augment(
  Bike_data_rain_lm_engine)

ggplot(
  Bike_data_rain_lm_aug,
  aes(x = .fitted, y = .resid)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "red") +
  labs(
    title = "Residuals vs Fitted Values",
    x = "Fitted Values",
    y = "Residuals") +
  theme_minimal()


bike_data_rain %>%
  ggplot(aes(
    x = Temperature.蚓.,
    y = Rented.Bike.Count,
    colour = Precipitation)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  labs(
    title = "Bike Rentals Against Temperature by Precipitation",
    x = "Temperature",
    y = "Number of Bike Rentals",
    colour = "Precipitation") +
  theme_minimal()


Bike_data_rain_lm_interaction <- linear_reg() %>%
  set_engine("lm") %>%
  fit(
    Rented.Bike.Count ~ Temperature.蚓. * Precipitation,
    data = bike_data_rain)

tidy(Bike_data_rain_lm_interaction)

glance(Bike_data_rain_lm_interaction)

```

```{r}

library(knitr)

Bike_data_rain <- bike_data %>%
  select(
    Temperature.蚓.,
    Rainfall.mm.,
    Snowfall..cm.,
    Rented.Bike.Count) %>%
  drop_na() %>%
  mutate(
    Precipitation = case_when(
      Rainfall.mm. > 0 | Snowfall..cm. > 0 ~ "Precipitation",
      TRUE ~ "No Precipitation"),
    Precipitation = factor(
      Precipitation,
      levels = c("No Precipitation", "Precipitation")))

set.seed(1234)

Bike_data_rain_split <- initial_split(Bike_data_rain)

Bike_data_rain_train <- training(Bike_data_rain_split)
Bike_data_rain_test  <- testing(Bike_data_rain_split)

Bike_data_rain_rec_1 <- recipe(
  Precipitation ~ Temperature.蚓.,
  data = Bike_data_rain_train
)

Bike_data_rain_mod_1 <- logistic_reg() %>%
  set_engine("glm")

Bike_data_rain_wflow_1 <- workflow() %>%
  add_model(Bike_data_rain_mod_1) %>%
  add_recipe(Bike_data_rain_rec_1)

Bike_data_rain_fit_1 <- Bike_data_rain_wflow_1 %>%
  fit(data = Bike_data_rain_train)

tidy(Bike_data_rain_fit_1)

bike_data_rain_pred_1 <- predict(
  Bike_data_rain_fit_1,
  Bike_data_rain_test,
  type = "prob"
)

bike_data_rain_pred_1 <- bind_cols(
  Bike_data_rain_test %>% select(Precipitation),
  bike_data_rain_pred_1
)

bike_data_rain_pred_1 <- bind_cols(
  Bike_data_rain_test %>% select(Rainfall.mm.),
  bike_data_rain_pred_1
)


bike_data_rain_roc_1 <- bike_data_rain_pred_1 %>%
  roc_curve(
    truth = Precipitation,
    .pred_Precipitation,
    event_level = "second"
  )

autoplot(bike_data_rain_roc_1) +
  labs(
    title = "ROC Curve - Logistic Regression Model 1",
    x = "1 - Specificity (False Positive Rate)",
    y = "Sensitivity (True Positive Rate)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```
  

MODE DATA OF TIMES OF DAY 95% CONFIDENCE INTERVAL THROUGH BOOTSRAPPING - MODE HOURS IN THE MORNING AND AFTERNOON FOR BIKE RENTAL

```{r}
library(infer)
daily_modes <- bike_data %>%
  mutate(
    Time_Period = if_else(Hour < 12, "AM", "PM")
  ) %>%
  group_by(Date, Time_Period) %>%
  slice_max(
    order_by = Rented.Bike.Count,
    n = 1,
    with_ties = FALSE
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(Date, Time_Period, Mode_Hour = Hour)

daily_modes

set.seed(1234)

bootstrap_means <- daily_modes %>%
  group_by(Time_Period) %>%
  summarise(
    Sample_Means = list(
      replicate(
        1500,
        mean(
          sample(
            Mode_Hour,
            size = n(),
            replace = TRUE
          )
        )
      )
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

bootstrap_summary <- bootstrap_means %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    Mean_of_Sample_Means = mean(Sample_Means),
    SD_of_Sample_Means = sd(Sample_Means)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

bootstrap_summary

bootstrap_summary <- bootstrap_summary %>%
  mutate(
    Lower_CI = Mean_of_Sample_Means -
      1.96 * SD_of_Sample_Means,

    Upper_CI = Mean_of_Sample_Means +
      1.96 * SD_of_Sample_Means
  )

bootstrap_summary

bootstrap_means %>%
  unnest(Sample_Means) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Sample_Means)) +
  geom_histogram(
    aes(y = after_stat(density)),
    bins = 30
  ) +
  geom_density(linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~Time_Period, scales = "free") +
  labs(
    title = "Sampling Distribution of Mean Peak Rental Hours",
    x = "Mean Peak Rental Hour",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


```
